status: Architectural review and executed control only; compiler and Gdev source unchanged.
verdict: Primarily a compiler backend representation problem. Ordinary records, borrows and helper calls should not need source rewrites to accommodate eager physical materialization.
distinction: local.get/set are Wasm operand/local operations, not heap loads/stores. Percentage of bytes alone is not a removability or runtime cost proof.

evidence.mechanism: Scalar values become physical locals immediately
evidence.finding: Constants allocate/set locals; primitive operations emit their result into another local. Later consumers load those locals. Code.value already supports nested stack expressions. Ordinary scalar bindings without scalar addresses already share their original Value, so not every binding creates a copy.

evidence.mechanism: Recursive aggregate transport and coarse loop carries
evidence.finding: Snapshot/temporary/assignment recurse through physical fields and owner metadata. Loop invariance is chosen per whole aggregate; changing one field can still snapshot and assign the whole carrier at the emitted boundary.

evidence.mechanism: Outlining amplifies local pressure into a global bank
evidence.finding: Outlined regions use no-argument/no-result helpers. Cross-region locals become mutable globals, root entry resets them, and banked tee becomes global.set plus global.get. Local compaction occurs after bank selection.

executed_scalar_control.workload: 16 successive multiply/xor pairs over a dynamic U32 input; 32 arithmetic operations and identical constants in both emitted bodies. Zero-operation controls subtract each ABI/function scaffold.
executed_scalar_control.finding: The 254-byte difference in incremental computational body size is entirely local-variable traffic; arithmetic and constant bytes match.
executed_scalar_control.limits: A small output-quality control, not a whole-language throughput benchmark or an estimate of whole-game savings. Local operations are not heap memory accesses.

ranked_experiments.direction: Separate logical values from physical storage in the existing backend
ranked_experiments.experiment: Single-use versus reused scalar chains, and width/changed-lane loop controls. Keep immediates and single-use expressions on the operand stack where order permits; materialize only actual mutable/reused/escaping lanes.

ranked_experiments.direction: Compare scalarized and addressed representations at large aggregate boundaries
ranked_experiments.experiment: The same 32/128-field programs with identity return, one-field update and full update, including shared and distinct owners. Small records remain scalarized. Measure memory operations and execution as well as code size.

ranked_experiments.direction: Give outlined regions live input/output interfaces instead of an unbounded global bank
ranked_experiments.experiment: A small fixture crossing the outline threshold; compare real parameters/results for narrow interfaces and scoped frames for wide interfaces. Measure code, bank/frame slots, initialization and repeated invocation behavior.
preserve: no invalid reentrancy or shared-bank cycles

architecture: Core already has single-assignment bindings, merges and loop carries, plus a typed stack IR. Add value identity/demand/def-use information or a small virtual-word representation first. A whole new frontend or large semantic IR is not justified by this review.
limits: No quantified removable fraction of the 9.48MB local/global instructions.
No demonstrated path from13.94MB to1–2MB yet.
No proof that reducing instruction count alone fixes 5.6s compiler latency.
Current stripped Wasm lacks per-instruction source attribution; function indices from different frozen builds must not be equated.
Historical 2.08MB heap-record output used different source/APIs/memory model, so it motivates a controlled representation test, not a promised gain.
